acceptance_criteria.description: A bounded Codex Windows/local read-only inventory exposes only source-bound non-sensitive MCP definitions and preserves /mcp compatibility; malformed, duplicate, empty, and secret-bearing inputs have focused tests.
Explicit Codex mcptoolcall activity is bounded and redacted, while absent attribution remains generic; focused projection tests pass.

Project-local MCP profile lifecycle is additive in the existing Workbench TOML store, preserves prior state on failure, keeps same-name definitions source-bound, and never writes provider configuration or secrets.
The Agents surface provides accessible inventory/profile/unsupported states, keyboard and focus behavior, truthful passive status, and inert rendering with focused UI tests.
The public Rust/TypeScript contract remains additive and generated parity, focused Rust tests, and focused frontend tests pass without unrelated edits or speculative infrastructure.

closed_decisions: Implement only Codex Windows/local read-only inventory, project-local profiles, explicit MCP activity attribution, and the truthful Agents surface admitted by the package.
Preserve the existing /mcp compatibility entry point and all prior Workbench TOML behavior.
Provider-derived values are untrusted, bounded, normalized, redacted, and inert.
Unsupported provider and target behavior remains visibly unsupported; do not invent a provider abstraction.
No provider-file write, imported-command execution, network probe, WSL copy, launcher restart, credential storage, new persistence service, daemon, database, MCP client, or proxy is authorized.
Use the generated-contract workflow for src/bus/contract.generated.ts rather than hand-editing it.
Keep the implementation direct and inside existing seams; YAGNI, KISS, and current project conventions govern.
Do not touch the root-owned E2E cleanup fix, Seneschal packet, queue, approval receipt, roadmap, or native audit evidence.

natural: Run formatting checks limited to owned Rust, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, and child-state files when repository tooling supports it.

forbidden_changes: Do not add a generic provider framework, adapter registry, daemon, service, database, polling layer, MCP client/proxy, marketplace, cloud sync, credential vault, or automatic server launcher.
Do not implement non-Codex or WSL imports, provider synchronization, active connectivity probes, launcher application, session restart, or provider-file mutation.
Do not expose or persist args, env, headers, credentials, raw tool payloads, arbitrary URLs, or raw provider paths in bus/UI/journal data.
Do not edit scripts/run-tauri-e2e.mjs, approved planning/roadmap/swarm artifacts, queue state, approval receipts, package manifests, lockfiles, branches, commits, PRs, Jira, or release state.
Do not delete or rewrite existing user changes outside the owned file list.
objective: Implement the execution-ready RDM-024 U1-U3 slice end to end using the existing Agent Console, Workbench TOML, bus, and Agents UI seams.
